Alternative forms

[edit]
  • piè (clipping)

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin pedem (“foot”), from Proto-Indo-European *pṓds. Compare Catalan peu, French pied, Piedmontese pé, Latvian pēda, Lithuanian pėdės, Portuguese pé, Sardinian pei, Spanish pie.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpjɛ.de/, /ˈpje.de/[1]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛde, -ede
  • Hyphenation: piè‧de, pié‧de

Noun

[edit]

piede m (plural piedi, diminutive piedìno, augmentative piedóne, pejorative piedàccio, diminutive-endearing piedùccio)

  1. foot

Derived terms

[edit]
  • appiedare
  • piedino
  • piedistallo
  • su due piedi
  • marciapiede

Related terms

[edit]
  • pedale
  • pedestre
  • pedone
  • pedule

References

[edit]
  1. ^ piede in Luciano Canepari, Dizionario di Pronuncia Italiana (DiPI)

Walloon

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Old French perdre, from Latin perdō, perdere (“loose”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /pjɛt/

Verb

[edit]

piede

  1. to lose
